transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know, I've been asked to restore a worn 1920s community cookbook that has a detached cover and several loose pages. Before I decide whether to accept this commission and set the final terms, I'd like to hear from anyone who has terms, offers, or material constraints they think I should know about. Please, go ahead.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I'd like to propose a barter arrangement. Inez, if you'll reattach the cover, resew the loose sections, and make a simple cloth spine for the cookbook, I'll provide twelve archival linen sheets plus $40. I'll bring the book Tuesday at 18:00 and collect it Saturday at 16:00.

transcript.text: I'd like to put an offer on the table as well. I've offered Inez $320 cash for a separate two-week restoration of a family recipe ledger, and that offer remains open.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I inspected this cookbook for a local archivist, who confirmed that its brittle acidic pages require wheat-starch paste and Japanese tissue for the loose-page repairs; ordinary PVA glue should not be used.
